correctness.rationale: The multiplicity-two domain is exhaustively p^2 or pq. Prime squares are impossible by coprimality. For pq, the identity phi(pq)=(p-1)(p+q+1)-(p-1)(p+2) gives a bidirectional equivalence between s(pq)|phi(pq) and p+q+1|(p-1)(p+2); q>p is exactly the divisor-size condition. The verifier corroborates, but does not establish, the universal proof.

value.rationale: The theorem completely resolves the first nontrivial composite multiplicity layer of a published arithmetic-function divisibility problem. It turns semiprime membership into an exact divisor test for each smaller prime, explains the early database examples, and subsumes the known Dickson-conditional family without relying on bounded enumeration.
